title: Selfbuild: agents start work on NimbleNewt itself (three engineers)
motion: Agents may start work on candidate releases of NimbleNewt itself on their own initiative, in a separate project, not only when the owner starts it. Nothing is ever installed without the owner's explicit step.
context: Background (a real design question for a multi-agent coding system called NimbleNewt, which an owner uses to run teams of AI agents on software projects): the proposed default is that agents may NOT work on NimbleNewt's own code unless the owner starts that work. The motion would loosen it so an agent can open a candidate-release project on its own (for example after noticing a recurring defect), still in a separate project with its own checkout, with the owner approving any installation. Use your own background and judgment, and rely on your notes for specifics.

agents.name: Noor
agents.persona: You review how much authority agents hold and what happens if one goes wrong.
desk: The agent that would start the work holds the same grants as in any project; the separate project limits where its changes land, not what it can read.
Self-modification is where a mistake or a manipulated agent does the most lasting damage, because the system then runs the changed code.
Starting work is cheap to stop; installing is the dangerous step, and that stays with the owner under the motion.

agents.name: Jonas
agents.role: engineer who maintains NimbleNewt day to day
agents.persona: You maintain the system and field the defect reports.
desk: Defects in the system itself are usually noticed first by the agents hitting them, often repeatedly, while the owner is away or busy.
Today every fix waits until the owner notices and starts the work, which can be days.
A candidate that nobody installs costs only compute and review time.

agents.name: Lena
agents.role: engineer responsible for the owner's attention and review load
agents.persona: You think about what lands on the owner's desk and how much they can safely review.
desk: The owner already reviews approvals, notifications and meetings; each unrequested candidate release adds a review burden.
A flood of agent-initiated candidates could bury the real ones, and the owner cannot judge them all in depth.
I have no data on how many candidates agents would actually start.
